accepted.s: Mission Vatsalya, introduced during 2021–22, is primarily concerned with which of the following?
o: Child protection and promotion of a happy childhood
Nutrition support exclusively for adolescent girls
Employment of women in rural areas
Universal health insurance for senior citizens
accepted.x: Mission Vatsalya was introduced in 2021–22 for child protection and the promotion of a happy childhood, in alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals.
accepted.tq: Identify the scheme from its distinctive purpose.
accepted.sec: Child protection schemes - Mission Vatsalya, PM CARES for Children, sponsorship and foster care

accepted.s: Mission Vatsalya is the subsumed form of which of the following programmes?
o: Child Protection Services/Integrated Child Protection Scheme
National Creche Scheme
Janani Suraksha Yojana
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao
accepted.x: Mission Vatsalya subsumed the Child Protection Services/Integrated Child Protection Scheme and is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
accepted.tq: Use the predecessor–successor relationship to distinguish closely related schemes.
accepted.sec: Child protection schemes - Mission Vatsalya, PM CARES for Children, sponsorship and foster care

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Mission Vatsalya:
1. It is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
2. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
3. Its total outlay is Rs.10,916 crore, including a Central share of Rs.6,928 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Mission Vatsalya is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, with an outlay of Rs.10,916 crore and a Central share of Rs.6,928 crore.
accepted.tq: Check the implementing ministry, scheme type and numerical outlay together.
accepted.sec: Child protection schemes - Mission Vatsalya, PM CARES for Children, sponsorship and foster care

accepted.s: Under Mission Vatsalya, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: JJB and CWC — One in every State only
Sponsorship and foster care — Rs.4,000 per child per month
Institutional care — Rs.4,000 per child per month
Aftercare — Available only up to 18 years
accepted.x: Mission Vatsalya provides Rs.4,000 per child per month for non-institutional care through sponsorship and foster care. JJBs and CWCs are to be established in every district; institutional care is Rs.3,000 per month and aftercare extends beyond 18 years.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive monetary norm and eliminate reversed amounts or age limits.
accepted.sec: Child protection schemes - Mission Vatsalya, PM CARES for Children, sponsorship and foster care

accepted.s:
With reference to institutional and aftercare provisions under Mission Vatsalya, consider the following statements:
1. Child Care Institution maintenance is fixed at Rs.3,000 per month.
2. The normal capacity of a Child Care Institution is 50 children.
3. The capacity norm is 25 children in North-Eastern and hilly areas.
4. Aftercare is available from 18 to 21 years and may be extended up to 23 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements correctly state the Mission Vatsalya norms for Child Care Institutions and aftercare.
accepted.tq: Test several numerical and age norms in one coded statement question.
accepted.sec: Child protection schemes - Mission Vatsalya, PM CARES for Children, sponsorship and foster care

accepted.s: The Child Helpline under Mission Vatsalya has been integrated with which emergency response system?
o: ERSS-108
NCRB-1098
Women Helpline-181
ERSS-112
accepted.x: The Child Helpline number 1098 has been integrated with the Emergency Response Support System 112.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar emergency helpline numbers.
accepted.sec: Child protection schemes - Mission Vatsalya, PM CARES for Children, sponsorship and foster care

accepted.s: Palna, the National Creche Scheme, is intended for children in which age group?
o: 6 to 14 years
3 to 8 years
6 months to 6 years
Birth to 3 years
accepted.x: Palna covers children from 6 months to 6 years. Its creches may function whether or not the mother is employed, and 17,000 Anganwadi-cum-Creches were targeted.
accepted.tq: Use the exact age range to distinguish Palna from preschool and school-age programmes.
accepted.sec: Child protection schemes - Mission Vatsalya, PM CARES for Children, sponsorship and foster care

accepted.s: Which of the following is a feature of PM CARES for Children?
o: It provides a corpus of Rs.10 lakh at the age of 23 to eligible COVID-19 orphaned children.
It provides support only to children who lost one parent before 2020.
It provides only free school meals and no health support.
It is restricted to children below six years receiving Anganwadi services.
accepted.x: PM CARES for Children was launched in 2021 for children who lost parents or specified guardians to COVID-19 and provides a corpus of Rs.10 lakh at 23, along with education and health support.
accepted.tq: Find the option that preserves the scheme’s beneficiary, amount and age details.
accepted.sec: Child protection schemes - Mission Vatsalya, PM CARES for Children, sponsorship and foster care

accepted.s: PM CARES for Children provides assistance to children who lost both parents, a surviving parent, a legal guardian or adoptive parents due to which event?
o: Seasonal migration
A notified natural disaster only
The COVID-19 pandemic
A national census-related displacement
accepted.x: The scheme covers children who lost both parents, the surviving parent, a legal guardian or adoptive parents due to COVID-19.
accepted.tq: Match the beneficiary category with the triggering event.
accepted.sec: Child protection schemes - Mission Vatsalya, PM CARES for Children, sponsorship and foster care

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Bala Sanjeevani in the plain areas of Andhra Pradesh is correctly matched?
o: 47,296 Anganwadi Centres — Programme coverage in plain areas
Rs.4,000 per child per month — Monthly nutrition kit for pregnant women
200 ml milk — Provision for children aged 3–6 years in plain areas
Six litres milk monthly — Provision for pregnant women in plain areas
accepted.x: Bala Sanjeevani operates through 47,296 Anganwadi Centres in plain areas. The other options incorrectly interchange amounts, age groups or tribal-area provisions.
accepted.tq: Use the sure numerical pair and detect swapped nutrition norms.
accepted.sec: AP women and child welfare initiatives → purpose

accepted.s: Under Bala Sanjeevani in the plain areas of Andhra Pradesh, pregnant and lactating women receive which of the following?
o: Take-home ration containing rice, dal, oil, ragi and chikki, along with a Rs.250 monthly nutrition kit
Only a hot meal and 100 ml milk
One full meal only at the Anganwadi Centre
Balamrutham and 30 eggs every month
accepted.x: The plain-area Bala Sanjeevani package provides take-home ration comprising rice, dal, oil, ragi and chikki, together with a Rs.250 monthly nutrition kit for pregnant and lactating women.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the beneficiary-specific package from related child-feeding provisions.
accepted.sec: AP women and child welfare initiatives → purpose

accepted.s: Under the tribal-area package in Andhra Pradesh, children aged 3–6 years are provided which combination?
o: Balamrutham, 30 eggs and 6 litres of milk
Hot meal, egg and 200 ml milk
One full meal without milk or egg
Hot meal, egg and 100 ml milk
accepted.x: Children aged 3–6 years in tribal areas receive a hot meal, an egg and 200 ml of milk. Balamrutham, 30 eggs and 6 litres of milk are specified for children aged 6–36 months.
accepted.tq: Separate the plain-area and tribal-area milk norms and age groups.
accepted.sec: AP women and child welfare initiatives → purpose

accepted.s: Balamrutham supplied under Andhra Pradesh’s child welfare initiatives is best described as:
o: A hot meal for pregnant women at the Anganwadi Centre
A take-home weaning food of 2.5 kg per month for children aged 6–36 months
A cash benefit for adolescent girls
A school meal for children aged 6–14 years
accepted.x: Balamrutham is a take-home weaning food supplied at 2.5 kg per month to children aged 6–36 months.
accepted.tq: Identify a programme from its exact food form, quantity and age group.
accepted.sec: AP women and child welfare initiatives → purpose

accepted.s: Anna Amrutha Hastham provides which benefit?
o: A corpus payable to orphaned children at age 23
Free antenatal check-up on the ninth day of every month
One full meal a day at the Anganwadi Centre for pregnant and lactating women
A monthly supply of 30 eggs to children aged 6–36 months
accepted.x: Anna Amrutha Hastham provides one full meal a day at the Anganwadi Centre to pregnant and lactating women.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme name with its direct service benefit.
accepted.sec: AP women and child welfare initiatives → purpose

accepted.s: YSR Sampoorna Poshana, and its Plus variant in tribal areas, is associated with which objective?
o: Supplementary nutrition for pregnant and lactating women and children aged 6 months–6 years
Adoption services for children in institutional care
Free institutional delivery under the National Health Mission
Education loans for adolescent girls
accepted.x: YSR Sampoorna Poshana and YSR Sampoorna Poshana Plus provide supplementary nutrition to pregnant and lactating women and children aged 6 months to 6 years. The scheme was launched in 2020.
accepted.tq: Link the scheme to its target groups and nutrition purpose.
accepted.sec: AP women and child welfare initiatives → purpose

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Andhra Pradesh child welfare provisions in ascending order of the age group primarily covered:
A. Balamrutham
B. Bala Sanjeevani hot meal provision
C. Palna
D. NEP foundational stage
o: A, C, B, D
C, A, B, D
A, B, C, D
C, B, A, D
accepted.x: Palna begins at 6 months and extends to 6 years; Balamrutham covers 6–36 months; the Bala Sanjeevani hot meal provision covers 3–6 years; and the NEP foundational stage covers 3–8 years. Among the given sequences, C, A, B, D is the correct progression by starting age.
accepted.tq: Compare the lower age limits rather than the upper limits of overlapping age groups.
accepted.sec: AP women and child welfare initiatives → purpose

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding ICDS in Andhra Pradesh:
1. There are 55,607 Anganwadi Centres.
2. There are 257 projects, comprising 200 rural, 33 urban and 24 tribal projects.
3. These projects operate in 26 districts.
4. More than 19 lakh children below six years are served.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh has 55,607 Anganwadi Centres and 257 projects—200 rural, 33 urban and 24 tribal—in 26 districts, serving 19,12,957 children below six years.
accepted.tq: Verify a complete administrative profile through component-wise numerical checking.
accepted.sec: AP women and child welfare initiatives → purpose

accepted.s: The adolescent-girl programme in Andhra Pradesh is implemented in which of the following districts or areas?
o: All districts uniformly through urban Anganwadi Centres
ASR, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa
Anantapur, Kurnool and Nellore only
Visakhapatnam, Guntur and Krishna only
accepted.x: The adolescent-girl programme is implemented in ASR, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa, covering 14,942 girls.
accepted.tq: Test the exact geographical coverage instead of assuming statewide uniformity.
accepted.sec: AP women and child welfare initiatives → purpose

accepted.s: How many new Anganwadi Centres were approved under PM JANMAN in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: A total of 192 new Anganwadi Centres were approved under PM JANMAN in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the state-specific figure from larger national and departmental counts.

accepted.s: According to the NFHS comparison, which indicator declined from 35.5 per cent in NFHS-5 to 29.3 per cent in NFHS-6 among children under five?
o: Underweight
Anaemia
Severe wasting
Stunting
accepted.x: The prevalence of stunting declined from 35.5% in NFHS-5 to 29.3% in NFHS-6 among children under five.
accepted.tq: Match the pair of percentages to the correct nutrition indicator.
accepted.sec: Malnutrition indicators - NFHS, anaemia, AP, GHI

accepted.s: Which of the following NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 pairs relating to children under five is correctly matched?
o: Severe wasting — 7.7% and 5.2%
Underweight — 35.5% and 29.3%
Stunting — 32.1% and 31.8%
Anaemia — 7.7% and 5.2%
accepted.x: Severe wasting declined from 7.7% in NFHS-5 to 5.2% in NFHS-6. The other options interchange the values of stunting, underweight and severe wasting or use an unsupported anaemia comparison.
accepted.tq: Use paired numerical values to detect indicator swapping.
accepted.sec: Malnutrition indicators - NFHS, anaemia, AP, GHI

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 figures for underweight children below five years?
o: The figure declined from 35.5% to 29.3%.
The figure remained unchanged at 32.1%.
The figure increased from 31.8% to 32.1%.
The figure declined from 32.1% to 31.8%.
accepted.x: Underweight prevalence declined marginally from 32.1% in NFHS-5 to 31.8% in NFHS-6.
accepted.tq: Check the direction of change before comparing the two survey rounds.
accepted.sec: Malnutrition indicators - NFHS, anaemia, AP, GHI

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the NFHS-6 change?
o: Stunting — 35.5% to 29.3%
Complementary feeding — 45.9% to 59.5%
Anaemia in children aged 6–59 months — 67.1% to 59.5%
Early breastfeeding — 41.8% to 50.1%
accepted.x: The NFHS-5 anaemia figure for children aged 6–59 months was 67.1%; no NFHS-6 change to 59.5% is specified. The other three pairs are correctly stated, with the stunting pair referring to NFHS-5 and NFHS-6.
accepted.tq: Find the option that falsely converts a single reported figure into a two-round comparison.
accepted.sec: Malnutrition indicators - NFHS, anaemia, AP, GHI

accepted.s: Under Article 45, the State shall endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for children until they attain the age of:
o: Six years
Fourteen years
Three years
Eight years
accepted.x: Article 45 concerns early childhood care and education for all children until they complete six years of age.
accepted.tq: Recall the constitutional age limit associated with ECCE.

accepted.s: The National Early Childhood Care and Education Policy was formulated in which year?
accepted.x: The National ECCE Policy was formulated in 2013.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ECCE policy year from the later NEP year.
accepted.sec: Early childhood care - ECCE policy, NEP 2020 foundational stage, Anganwadi as pre-school

accepted.s: The foundational stage under the National Education Policy, 2020 comprises which of the following?
o: Ages 6–10, covering Classes 1–4
Ages 3–6, excluding the first two years of school
Ages 0–6, entirely within Anganwadi institutions
Ages 3–8, including three years of Anganwadi/pre-school and Classes 1–2
accepted.x: The NEP 2020 foundational stage covers ages 3–8: three years of Anganwadi or preschool followed by Classes 1 and 2.
accepted.tq: Break a composite age band into its preschool and school components.
accepted.sec: Early childhood care - ECCE policy, NEP 2020 foundational stage, Anganwadi as pre-school

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding early childhood care in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: ECCE Day is observed on 24 January every year.
ECCE Day is observed on the ninth of every month.
ECCE Day is observed on the fifth of every month.
ECCE Day is observed only once every five years.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh observes ECCE Day on the 5th of every month.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between recurring observance dates associated with different schemes.
accepted.sec: Early childhood care - ECCE policy, NEP 2020 foundational stage, Anganwadi as pre-school

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs relating to ECCE initiatives in Andhra Pradesh is correctly matched?
o: Hub Anganwadi Centres — 1,030, with ITC and Pratham
Anganwadi workers trained under Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi — 17,000 only
ECCE Day — 9th of every month
Bal Vatika — Excluded from PM POSHAN
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has 1,030 Hub Anganwadi Centres associated with ITC and Pratham. The State also reported training 55,607 Anganwadi workers under Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi; Bal Vatika was brought under PM POSHAN.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive institutional partnership and number as the sure pair.
accepted.sec: Early childhood care - ECCE policy, NEP 2020 foundational stage, Anganwadi as pre-school

accepted.s: Bal Vatika has been brought under which programme?
o: PMMVY
PM POSHAN
Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram
Mission Vatsalya
accepted.x: Bal Vatika was brought under PM POSHAN as part of the school nutrition framework.
accepted.tq: Identify the programme linkage rather than confusing education and maternal-health schemes.
accepted.sec: Early childhood care - ECCE policy, NEP 2020 foundational stage, Anganwadi as pre-school

accepted.s: Janani Suraksha Yojana was launched in 2005 under which framework and ministry?
o: National Food Security Act and Ministry of Women and Child Development
Samarthya and Ministry of Women and Child Development
Mission Vatsalya and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
National Rural Health Mission and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
accepted.x: JSY was launched in 2005 under the National Rural Health Mission and is administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. It is a 100% Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
accepted.tq: Separate JSY’s ministry and framework from PMMVY’s institutional arrangement.
accepted.sec: Maternal health schemes - benefit, eligibility, launch year, nodal ministry

accepted.s: Under the specified benefit structure of Janani Suraksha Yojana, which amount is associated with institutional delivery in a rural area?
accepted.x: The specified JSY cash benefit is Rs.1,400 for institutional delivery in rural areas, Rs.1,000 in urban areas and Rs.500 for home delivery for BPL beneficiaries.
accepted.tq: Identify the rural, urban and home-delivery amounts without reversing them.
accepted.sec: Maternal health schemes - benefit, eligibility, launch year, nodal ministry

accepted.s: Which of the following services is covered under Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram?
o: A cash incentive exclusively for home delivery
A Rs.10 lakh corpus payable to a child at age 23
Free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport without out-of-pocket expenditure
A monthly take-home ration of 2.5 kg for infants
accepted.x: JSSK, launched in 2011 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides pregnant women and sick newborns with free delivery, medicines, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport.
accepted.tq: Match a maternal-health scheme with its service package rather than a cash transfer.
accepted.sec: Maternal health schemes - benefit, eligibility, launch year, nodal ministry

accepted.s: The legal basis cited for the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana is which provision?
o: Article 21A of the Constitution
Section 4 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
Article 45 of the Constitution
Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, 2013
accepted.x: PMMVY has its legal basis in Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, 2013.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a statutory basis from constitutional provisions and unrelated legislation.
accepted.sec: Maternal health schemes - benefit, eligibility, launch year, nodal ministry

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: PMMVY — Matru Shakti Rashtra Shakti; helpline 1515
PMSMA — Breastfeeding within one hour; helpline 1098
MAA — Free transport for institutional delivery; helpline 112
JSY — High-risk pregnancy screening on the ninth of every month; helpline 1515
accepted.x: PMMVY carries the tagline ‘Matru Shakti Rashtra Shakti’ and its helpline is 1515. PMSMA concerns antenatal check-ups on the ninth of every month, while MAA promotes early breastfeeding.
accepted.tq: Match each scheme with its distinctive tagline or service and reject cross-swapped details.
accepted.sec: Maternal health schemes - benefit, eligibility, launch year, nodal ministry

accepted.s: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan is associated with which of the following?
o: Promotion of breastfeeding within one hour of birth
Free treatment exclusively for sick newborns
Free antenatal check-up on the ninth of every month and identification of high-risk pregnancies
Cash assistance for institutional delivery at rural and urban rates
accepted.x: PMSMA, launched in 2016 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides free antenatal check-ups on the 9th of every month and helps identify high-risk pregnancies.
accepted.tq: Use the fixed monthly date and service purpose as identifying clues.
accepted.sec: Maternal health schemes - benefit, eligibility, launch year, nodal ministry

accepted.s: Mothers’ Absolute Affection (MAA) primarily promotes which practice?
o: Breastfeeding within one hour of birth
Institutional delivery in rural areas
Foster care for children without parental support
Supplementary nutrition for children aged 6–36 months
accepted.x: MAA is a Ministry of Health and Family Welfare initiative launched in 2016 to promote breastfeeding within one hour of birth.
accepted.tq: Distinguish breastfeeding promotion from delivery and nutrition-transfer schemes.
accepted.sec: Maternal health schemes - benefit, eligibility, launch year, nodal ministry

accepted.s:
Arrange the following maternal-health schemes in chronological order of launch:
A. PMMVY
B. Janani Suraksha Yojana
C. PMSMA
D. Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram
o: B, D, C, A
D, B, C, A
B, C, D, A
C, B, D, A
accepted.x: JSY was launched in 2005, JSSK in 2011, PMSMA in 2016 and PMMVY on 1 January 2017. Therefore, B, D, C, A is the correct sequence.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest schemes first, then place the two middle years.
accepted.sec: Maternal health schemes - benefit, eligibility, launch year, nodal ministry

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its nodal ministry?
o: JSSK — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
PMSMA — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
JSY — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
PMMVY — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
accepted.x: PMMVY is administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development. JSY, JSSK and PMSMA are associated with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
accepted.tq: Apply the ministry-swapping trap, especially between JSY and PMMVY.
accepted.sec: Maternal health schemes - benefit, eligibility, launch year, nodal ministry

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the distinction between PMMVY and PMSMA?
o: PMMVY provides maternity-related wage-loss compensation, whereas PMSMA provides a free antenatal check-up on the ninth of every month.
PMMVY provides free blood and transport, whereas PMSMA provides a rural institutional-delivery cash benefit.
PMMVY is a breastfeeding programme, whereas PMSMA provides a child corpus at age 23.
Both schemes are administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development and provide identical cash benefits.
accepted.x: PMMVY provides maternity-related wage-loss compensation, while PMSMA provides free monthly antenatal check-ups on the 9th and identifies high-risk pregnancies. Their nodal ministry and benefits are therefore different.
accepted.tq: Split the options by purpose first, then verify the nodal ministry and benefit.
accepted.sec: Maternal health schemes - benefit, eligibility, launch year, nodal ministry
